blocks.text: Container root is constrained by a reduced capability set, a seccomp syscall filter and an LSM profile (AppArmor/SELinux); `--privileged` removes all three and exposes host devices, which makes it effectively host root.

rows: CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, SETUID, SETGID, KILL, NET_BIND_SERVICE, NET_RAW, SYS_CHROOT, MKNOD
SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, SYS_TIME, SYS_BOOT

items: A FastAPI service on port 8000 needs no capabilities.
Dropping NET_RAW (kept by default) blocks raw-packet spoofing on the bridge.
The default seccomp profile blocks kexec_load, reboot, init_module and more; `seccomp=unconfined` removes it.

rows: Rootless BuildKit, kaniko, Sysbox, remote builders

blocks.text:
# inside a privileged container:
# mount /dev/sda1 /mnt && chroot /mnt       → host filesystem as root

Q: "Why is --privileged dangerous?" A: "It grants all capabilities, disables seccomp and AppArmor/SELinux confinement and exposes host devices, so mounting the host disk is trivial. Use targeted --cap-add or --device instead, and default to --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges and a non-root user."

items: Drop ALL, add back only what's proven.
Devices and caps, not privileged mode.
